week_headline: Seed oils are dominating dinner table debates again, with viral posts claiming they are the root cause of modern disease — but the science tells a more measured story

top10.claim: Nutrition myth buster : How worried should you be about cooking with seed oils ?
top10.verdict: Seed oils like sunflower, canola, and soybean oil are not the silent killers some corners of the internet make them out to be — major health bodies including the WHO and American Heart Association still consider them preferable to saturated fats for heart health. There is a legitimate and ongoing scientific conversation about whether very high omega-6 intake relative to omega-3 may promote low-grade inflammation, but the evidence linking everyday cooking with seed oils to serious disease in humans is not strong or consistent. The real concern is overheating oils to their smoke point repeatedly, which can produce harmful compounds — so moderate heat and variety in your cooking fats is a sensible, evidence-grounded approach.
top10.verdict_highlight: Moderate use of seed oils is not a health crisis
sources: WHO – Fats and fatty acids in human nutrition (2010)
American Heart Association – Dietary Fats and Cardiovascular Disease (Circulation, 2017)
Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health – The Nutrition Source: Fats and Cholesterol
BMJ – Association of dietary linoleic acid with cardiovascular disease (2020)
Food Chemistry – Thermal degradation of cooking oils and formation of polar compounds (2019)
EFSA – Scientific opinion on dietary reference values for fats (2010)
top10.global_opinion: In the United States, seed oils have become politically charged, with some public health commentators and officials calling for their removal from the food supply despite mainstream dietetic bodies still endorsing them as heart-healthy swaps for saturated fat. In the UK, the NHS and British Dietetic Association maintain that unsaturated oils including seed oils are part of a balanced diet, and the debate has gained far less cultural traction. In parts of Southern Europe and the Mediterranean, olive oil dominates cooking culture and is strongly preferred on both traditional and scientific grounds, making the seed oil controversy feel largely irrelevant to everyday cooking habits there.
top10.brit_take: Most British kitchens have had a bottle of sunflower oil quietly sitting next to the hob for decades without incident — it turns out the chip pan was never the wholesome end of the story, but it was never a conspiracy either.
